headline: CVR Energy to buy two Marathon Midcontinent refineries for $4.2B
intro: While Washington digested a blue-wave midterm and Iran headlines kept oil traders on edge, the real refining news was a Midcontinent refinery swap: CVR is bulking up on Marathon's cast-offs just as diesel cracks sit north of $100/bbl.
overview: Crude slid for a third straight session as midterm election jitters and shifting Iran signals drove 2-3% losses across the petroleum complex, even as diesel cracks near $103/bbl keep refining margins historically rich. The big structural story is CVR Energy's $4.2 billion purchase of two Marathon refineries in Minnesota and North Dakota (177,000 bpd combined), alongside EIA data showing global refinery throughput clawing back from its Q2 Middle East-conflict-driven slump. On policy, EPA's SRE reallocation hearing drew support from both Clean Fuels Alliance and RFA, while New Jersey moved to block Russian diesel cargoes the Trump administration had cleared for import.

## Par Pacific (PARR) Q3 2026 — Refined Fuels Market Takeaways

- **Throughput down on planned maintenance, margins way up on crack spreads:** Total refining throughput fell to 174.2 Mbpd (vs. 197.7 Mbpd Q3'25) as Hawaii ran only 56.6 Mbpd (vs. 81.7 Mbpd) during a turnaround. Despite lower volumes, Adjusted Gross Margin/bbl more than doubled to $46.95 (vs. $24.76), and even excluding the SRE benefit, margin/bbl nearly tripled to $33.10 (vs. $13.62), reflecting a much stronger crack environment (Combined Index $38.45 vs. $14.72 y/y).

- **Capture rates diverged sharply by region:** Montana and Wyoming captured well above their regional index margins ex-SRE ($44.80 vs. $40.30 index; $51.91 vs. $49.83 index), while Hawaii's capture lagged materially ($20.69 AGM/bbl vs. $38.31 index) due to a $(10.03)/bbl negative price-lag impact from rising September product prices against prior-month/week contract pricing.

- **RIN/SRE exposure is large and one-time-ish:** EPA's August 2026 grant of full (100%) and partial (50%) small refinery exemptions for the 2025 compliance year added $187.2M to Adjusted Net Income and $222.0M to Adjusted EBITDA this quarter — concentrated in Montana ($167.2M benefit, $31.12/bbl) and smaller amounts in Washington ($32.2M, $8.66/bbl) and Wyoming ($22.6M, $13.07/bbl). Management expects to monetize the excess RIN position by year-end 2026, suggesting this tailwind normalizes going forward.
